newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai dissident wife requests visit,medical aid.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai dissident wife requests visit,medical aid.

text.p: The wife of jailed Shanghai dissident Yao Zhenxian said on Friday that she had written to the National People's Congress (parliament) to protest about his continued confinement, and demanded the right to see him.

Yao's wife, Zhang Yueyin, contacted by telephone, said she had not been allowed to see her husband since last October and that he and his brother Yao Zhenxiang were in poor health and were not receiving adequate medical attention.
"They should be allowed out to see a doctor," Zhang added.
The brothers, long-time supporters of the democracy movement in China, were both arrested in April last year and sent to a "reform through labour" camp in Jiangsu province north of Shanghai.
They were accused of illegally leaving China and distributing pornographic materials.
"We haven't been able to go and see them since last October. We want to be allowed to go and visit them," Zhang said.
Yao Zhenxiang fled to Hong Kong in 1994 and was granted political asylum in France. He returned to Shanghai in February last year after the police had promised not to arrest him.
The letter, sent to the parliament and to a human rights group in Hong Kong, called on the Chinese authorities to allow the brothers to appeal against their detention.
Under the terms of "reform through labour", people can be detained for up to three years without having to be sentenced in a court of law, at the discretion of the Public Security Bureau.
Officials could not be immediately contacted for comment.
